To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LL(d) scheduling policy has a limiting workload and response-time distribution that can be expressed in a simple closed form and that the LL(d)-policy is more effective than the classic power-of- d-choices in terms of response time.

the limiting workload distribution of the LL(d)-policy can be computed by solving a set of ordinary differential equation, that the limiting response time of LL(d)-scheduling is given by a simple closed form for exponential job sizes and can be computed via the unique solution to a set of ordinary different equation for phase-type distributed jobs, and that the LL(d)-algorithm outperforms the classic power-of-2-choices algorithm for all job size distributions considered.

the workload and response time distributions of the LL(d)-policy in large-scale homogeneous systems can be accurately approximated by a simple fixed-point iteration, which is based on a partial integro differential equation, for a wide variety of job size distributions.
